# Jhānavibhaṅga (Vb 12)

**ID:** Vb 12
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Jhānavibhaṅga
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul11.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In the broader framework of the *Vibhaṅga*, the text supplies analytical definitions and parameters for meditative absorptions and path factors, which intersect with analyses seen across related treatises such as the *Maggavibhaṅga* and *Saccavibhaṅga* [Anderson 1999]. In Pali commentarial tradition cited by Mrs. Rhys Davids, Buddhaghosa records a legend that the deva Kassapa heard the Buddha expound this text during his preaching of the Abhidhamma in Tāvatiṃsa heaven [Mrs. Rhys Davids 1917].

 DharmaNexus detects over 12,000 internal Pali text-reuse segments connecting the treatise to 266 texts, most substantially to other *Vibhaṅga* treatises including the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), *Appamaññāvibhaṅga* (Vb 13), *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 7), *Iddhipādavibhaṅga* (Vb 9), and *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), as well as parallel absorption matrices in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* and Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the treatise with northern Buddhist formulations of dhyāna and meditation stages in Sanskrit and Tibetan, including the *Śrāvakabhūmi* section of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā*, and large Prajñāpāramitā sūtras [DharmaNexus].
